title: Aviation mechanic privileges, recent experience and display practice questions
description: Practice questions on mechanic privileges and exclusions, recent experience, airframe and powerplant ratings, and certificate display (14 CFR 65.81–65.89).

questions.question: Under 14 CFR 65.81(a), what propeller work is excluded from a certificated mechanic's general privileges?

options.A: All maintenance of propellers
options.B: Major repairs to, and major alterations of, propellers
options.C: Preventive maintenance of propellers
options.D: Any work on propellers of light-sport aircraft

questions.explanation: A certificated mechanic may perform or supervise maintenance, preventive maintenance or alteration for which that person is rated, "but excluding major repairs to, and major alterations of, propellers".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.81, General privileges and limitations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: but excluding major repairs to, and major alterations of, propellers

questions.question: Under 14 CFR 65.81(a), what instrument work is excluded from a certificated mechanic's general privileges?

options.A: Only major repairs to instruments
options.B: Only major alterations of instruments
options.C: Only instrument work on aircraft used in air carrier service
options.D: Any repair to, or alteration of, instruments

questions.explanation: The exclusion in 65.81(a) covers "any repair to, or alteration of, instruments", not only major ones.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.81, General privileges and limitations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: and any repair to, or alteration of, instruments

questions.question: Under 14 CFR 65.81(a), on which aircraft or appliances may a certificated mechanic perform or supervise maintenance, preventive maintenance or alteration?

options.A: Those for which that person is rated, subject to the stated exclusions
options.B: Any aircraft or appliance, whatever the rating held
options.C: Only aircraft the mechanic owns
options.D: Only aircraft with a special airworthiness certificate

questions.explanation: The rule says a certificated mechanic may perform or supervise that work on "an aircraft or appliance, or a part thereof, for which that person is rated".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.81, General privileges and limitations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: of an aircraft or appliance, or a part thereof, for which that person is rated

questions.topic: Work not done before and manufacturer instructions
questions.question: Under 14 CFR 65.81(a), what must a certificated mechanic have done before supervising work on, or approving for return to service, an aircraft for which that person is rated?

options.A: Held the mechanic certificate for at least 30 months
options.B: Obtained an inspection authorization
options.C: Satisfactorily performed the work concerned at an earlier date
options.D: Obtained the aircraft owner's written consent

questions.explanation: A mechanic may not supervise that work or approve for return to service "unless that person has satisfactorily performed the work concerned at an earlier date."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.81, General privileges and limitations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: unless that person has satisfactorily performed the work concerned at an earlier date

questions.topic: Work not done before and manufacturer instructions
questions.question: A certificated mechanic has never performed a specific operation on an aircraft for which the mechanic is rated. Under 14 CFR 65.81(a), which is one way the mechanic may show the ability to do it?

options.A: Perform it under the direct supervision of a certificated and appropriately rated mechanic, or a certificated repairman, who has had previous experience in the specific operation concerned
options.B: Sign a statement that the mechanic has read about the operation
options.C: Perform it under the supervision of any pilot holding at least a private pilot certificate
options.D: Retake the written test for the rating

questions.explanation: The mechanic "may show the ability to do it by performing it to the satisfaction of the Administrator or under the direct supervision of a certificated and appropriately rated mechanic, or a certificated repairman, who has had previous experience in the specific operation concerned."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.81, General privileges and limitations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: that person may show the ability to do it by performing it to the satisfaction of the Administrator or under the direct supervision of a certificated and appropriately rated mechanic, or a certificated repairman, who has had previous experience in the specific operation concerned

questions.topic: Work not done before and manufacturer instructions
questions.question: Under 14 CFR 65.81(b), what must a certificated mechanic understand before exercising the privileges of the certificate and rating?

options.A: Only the aircraft flight manual
options.B: The current instructions of the manufacturer, and the maintenance manuals, for the specific operation concerned
options.C: The manufacturer's instructions as they stood when the aircraft was built
options.D: General textbooks for the type of work, in place of the manufacturer's instructions

questions.explanation: A mechanic may not exercise the privileges "unless that person understands the current instructions of the manufacturer, and the maintenance manuals, for the specific operation concerned."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.81, General privileges and limitations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: unless that person understands the current instructions of the manufacturer, and the maintenance manuals, for the specific operation concerned

questions.question: 14 CFR 65.83 measures a mechanic's recent experience over what period?

options.A: The preceding 90 days
options.B: The preceding 12 months
options.C: The preceding 5 years
options.D: The preceding 24 months

questions.explanation: A certificated mechanic may not exercise the privileges of his certificate and rating "unless, within the preceding 24 months" one of the conditions in 65.83(a) or (b) is met.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.83, Recent experience requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A certificated mechanic may not exercise the privileges of his certificate and rating unless, within the preceding 24 months

questions.question: What period of activity does 14 CFR 65.83(b) set within the 24-month look-back?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 6 months
options.D: 90 days

questions.explanation: Under 65.83(b), the mechanic must have, "for at least 6 months", been engaged in one of the listed activities or a combination of them.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.83, Recent experience requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: He has, for at least 6 months

questions.question: A certificated mechanic has done none of the activities listed in 14 CFR 65.83(b) in the preceding 24 months. What other condition in 65.83 lets the mechanic exercise the certificate's privileges?

options.A: The mechanic has renewed the certificate by mail
options.B: The mechanic holds at least a private pilot certificate
options.C: An employer has signed a statement of the mechanic's ability
options.D: Within the preceding 24 months, the Administrator has found that he is able to do that work

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a) is an alternative to (b): within the preceding 24 months, "The Administrator has found that he is able to do that work; or" the mechanic meets (b).

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.83, Recent experience requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The Administrator has found that he is able to do that work; or

questions.question: Which of these activities is listed in 14 CFR 65.83(b) as recent experience?

options.A: Technically supervising other mechanics
options.B: Flying as pilot in command
options.C: Holding a repairman certificate
options.D: Working as a flight instructor

questions.explanation: 65.83(b)(2) lists having "Technically supervised other mechanics".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.83, Recent experience requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Technically supervised other mechanics

questions.question: Under 14 CFR 65.83(b)(3), in what capacity may a mechanic have supervised the maintenance or alteration of aircraft for it to count as recent experience?

options.A: Only as an FAA inspector
options.B: In an executive capacity
options.C: Only while holding an inspection authorization
options.D: Only as an instructor at a part 147 school

questions.explanation: 65.83(b)(3) lists having "Supervised, in an executive capacity, the maintenance or alteration of aircraft".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.83, Recent experience requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Supervised, in an executive capacity, the maintenance or alteration of aircraft

questions.question: Within the preceding 24 months, a mechanic served as a mechanic under the certificate and rating for part of the time and technically supervised other mechanics for the rest. How does 14 CFR 65.83(b) treat a mix like this?

options.A: Only one activity, done without a break, counts
options.B: Only service as a mechanic under the certificate and rating counts
options.C: Being engaged in any combination of the activities in (b)(1), (2) or (3) counts
options.D: Only work on aircraft operated under part 121 counts

questions.explanation: 65.83(b)(4) counts having "Been engaged in any combination of paragraph (b) (1), (2), or (3) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.83, Recent experience requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Been engaged in any combination of paragraph (b) (1), (2), or (3) of this section

questions.question: Under 14 CFR 65.85(a), after which actions may a mechanic with an airframe rating approve an airframe, or any related part or appliance, for return to service?

options.A: Only after that person has personally performed the work
options.B: Only after a holder of an inspection authorization has inspected it
options.C: After that person has performed, supervised, or inspected its maintenance or alteration (excluding major repairs and major alterations)
options.D: After reviewing the owner's own logbook entry

questions.explanation: The airframe-rated mechanic may approve for return to service "after that person has performed, supervised, or inspected its maintenance or alteration (excluding major repairs and major alterations)."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.85, Airframe rating; additional privileges (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: after that person has performed, supervised, or inspected its maintenance or alteration (excluding major repairs and major alterations)

questions.question: Under 14 CFR 65.85(b), what must an airframe-rated mechanic have done with a major repair or major alteration on a light-sport category aircraft before approving the airframe for return to service?

options.A: Both performed and inspected it
options.B: Only supervised it
options.C: Only inspected it after another person performed it
options.D: Only recorded it after the owner performed it

questions.explanation: 65.85(b) allows that approval "after performing and inspecting a major repair or major alteration", so the mechanic must have done both.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.85, Airframe rating; additional privileges (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: after performing and inspecting a major repair or major alteration

questions.question: Under 14 CFR 65.85(a), after performing the 100-hour inspection required by part 91 on an airframe, what may an airframe-rated mechanic do?

options.A: Only recommend it to a holder of an inspection authorization for approval
options.B: Only record the work, leaving approval to a repair station
options.C: Approve it only after the Administrator reviews the inspection
options.D: Approve it for return to service

questions.explanation: An airframe-rated mechanic "may perform the 100-hour inspection required by part 91 of this chapter on an airframe, or any related part or appliance, and approve for return to service."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.85, Airframe rating; additional privileges (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: may perform the 100-hour inspection required by part 91 of this chapter on an airframe, or any related part or appliance, and approve for return to service

questions.question: 14 CFR 65.85(b) lets an airframe-rated mechanic approve an airframe for return to service after a major repair or major alteration in one stated case. To which aircraft and products does it apply?

options.A: Any aircraft with a standard airworthiness certificate
options.B: An aircraft with a special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category, for products that are not produced under an FAA approval
options.C: Any aircraft operated under part 135
options.D: Any aircraft the mechanic owns

questions.explanation: 65.85(b) covers "an aircraft with a special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category" and major repairs or alterations "for products that are not produced under an FAA approval".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.85, Airframe rating; additional privileges (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: of an aircraft with a special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category after performing and inspecting a major repair or major alteration for products that are not produced under an FAA approval

questions.question: A mechanic holds only a powerplant rating. Under 14 CFR 65.87(a), what may the mechanic approve for return to service after performing, supervising, or inspecting its maintenance or alteration (excluding major repairs and major alterations)?

options.A: A powerplant or propeller or any related part or appliance
options.B: An airframe, or any related part or appliance
options.C: Only engine accessories, not propellers
options.D: Instruments, after repairing them

questions.explanation: A powerplant-rated mechanic "may approve for return to service a powerplant or propeller or any related part or appliance" after that work.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.87, Powerplant rating; additional privileges (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: a certificated mechanic with a powerplant rating may approve for return to service a powerplant or propeller or any related part or appliance

questions.question: Under 14 CFR 65.87(b), a powerplant-rated mechanic may approve a powerplant or propeller of an aircraft with a special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category for return to service after a major repair or major alteration for products not produced under an FAA approval, provided the work met which condition?

options.A: It was approved in advance by the aircraft owner
options.B: It was performed by a student of a part 147 school
options.C: It was recorded on a form signed by the pilot
options.D: It was authorized by, and performed in accordance with instructions developed by, the manufacturer or a person acceptable to the FAA

questions.explanation: The approval is allowed "provided the major repair or major alteration was authorized by, and performed in accordance with instructions developed by, the manufacturer or a person acceptable to the FAA."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.87, Powerplant rating; additional privileges (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: provided the major repair or major alteration was authorized by, and performed in accordance with instructions developed by, the manufacturer or a person acceptable to the FAA

questions.question: Under 14 CFR 65.89, where must each person who holds a mechanic certificate keep it?

options.A: On file with the FAA
options.B: At home, in a safe place
options.C: Within the immediate area where he normally exercises the privileges of the certificate
options.D: In the aircraft's maintenance records

questions.explanation: Each holder "shall keep it within the immediate area where he normally exercises the privileges of the certificate".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.89, Display of certificate (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: shall keep it within the immediate area where he normally exercises the privileges of the certificate

questions.question: Under 14 CFR 65.89, who may request that a mechanic present the certificate for inspection?

options.A: The owner of an aircraft the mechanic worked on
options.B: An authorized representative of the National Transportation Safety Board
options.C: Any pilot holding at least a private pilot certificate
options.D: The mechanic's customers

questions.explanation: The holder "shall present it for inspection upon the request of the Administrator or an authorized representative of the National Transportation Safety Board, or of any Federal, State, or local law enforcement officer."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.89, Display of certificate (as of Nov 4, 2026)
